==English==

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵews-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|chois}}, from {{der|en|fro|chois|t=choice}}, from {{m|fro|choisir|t=to choose, perceive}}, possibly via assumed {{der|en|la-vul|*causīre|t=to choose}}, from {{der|en|got|𐌺𐌰𐌿𐍃𐌾𐌰𐌽|t=to make a choice, taste, test, choose}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*kauzijaną}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*keusaną|t=to choose}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ǵews-|t=to choose}}. Akin to {{cog|goh|kiosan|t=to choose}}, {{cog|ang|ċēosan|t=to choose}}, {{cog|non|kjósa|t=to choose}}. More at [[choose]].

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# An [[option]]; a [[decision]]; an opportunity to [[choose]] or [[select]] something.
#: {{syn|en|conclusion|opinion|verdict|call|Thesaurus:judgement}}
#: {{ux|en|Do I have a '''choice''' of what color to paint it?}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The power to choose.
#: {{ux|en|She didn't leave us much '''choice'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|title=Constitutional Government in the United States| author=w:Woodrow Wilson| year=1907| page=68| passage=For he is also the political leader of the nation, or has it in his '''choice''' to be.}}
# One [[selection]] or [[preference]]; that which is chosen or decided; the [[outcome]] of a [[decision]].
#: {{syn|en|option|possibility|Thesaurus:option}}
#: {{ux|en|The ice cream sundae is a popular '''choice''' for dessert.}}
# Anything that can be chosen.
#: {{syn|en|assortment|range|selection}}
#: {{ux|en|You have three '''choices''': vanilla, strawberry or chocolate.}}
# {{lb|en|usually|with ''the''}} The best or most preferable part.
#: {{syn|en|the [[cream]]}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Regained|3|passage=The flower and '''choice''' / Of many provinces from bound to bound.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Care and judgement in selecting; [[discrimination]], [[selectiveness]].
#* {{RQ:Bacon Apophthegmes|passage=I imagine they [the apothegms of Caesar] were collected with judgment and '''choice'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1757|author={{w|Edmund Burke}}|title={{w|A Philosophical Enquiry into the Origin of Our Ideas of the Sublime and Beautiful}}|location=London|publisher=R. & J. Dodsley|section=Part I, Section I, p. 1|url=https://archive.org/details/enqphilosophical00burkrich
|passage=We see children perpetually running from place to place to hunt out something new; they catch with great eagerness, and with very little '''choice''', at whatever comes before them; their attention is engaged by every thing, because every thing has, in that stage of life, the charm of novelty to recommend it.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A sufficient number to choose among.
#: {{syn|en|abundance|profusion|Thesaurus:cornucopia}}
# {{lb|en|set theory}} {{ellipsis of|en|axiom of choice}}.
#* {{quote-book|en
|url=https://books.google.ch/books?id=GIquDAAAQBAJ&lpg=PA51
|title=The Logical Foundations of Scientific Theories: Languages, Structures, and Models
|author=Decio Krause; Jonas R.B. Arenhart
|publisher=Routledge
|series=Routledge Studies in the Philosophy of Mathematics and Physics
|isbn=9781315535203
|date=2016-07-15
|page=51
|passage=5. ZF* is the theory obtained from the aforementioned axiomatics (without '''choice''') by adding the Axiom of Inaccessible Cardinals to be explained in the next secion; similarly, we get ZFC*.
}}

===Etymology 2===
From {{inh|en|enm|choys}}, from a merger of the noun above and {{inh|en|enm|chyse}}, {{m|enm|chuse}}, {{m|enm|chys}}, {{m|enm|chis|t=choice, excellent}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ċīes|t=choice; dainty; nice}}, related to {{cog|ang|ċēosan|t=to choose}}.

====Adjective====
{{en-adj|er,more}}

# Especially [[good]] or [[preferred]].
#: {{syn|en|prime|prize|quality|select|choicy}}
#: {{ux|en|It's a '''choice''' location, but you will pay more to live there.}}
#* {{RQ:Melville Moby-Dick|chapter=33|page=162|passage=This it is, that for ever keeps God’s true princes of the Empire from the world’s hustings; and leaves the highest honors that this air can give, to those men who become famous more through their infinite inferiority to the '''choice''' hidden handful of the Divine Inert, than through their undoubted superiority over the dead level of the mass.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Careful in choosing; discriminating.
#* {{RQ:Milton Areopagitica|text=that such iron moulds as these shall have autority to knaw out the '''choicest''' periods of exquisitest books, and to commit such a treacherous fraud against the orphan remainders of worthiest men after death, the more sorrow will belong to that haples race of men, whose misfortune it is to have understanding.}}
#* {{RQ:Wordsworth Resolution and Independence|passage='''Choice''' word, and measured phrase; above the reach / Of ordinary men; a stately speech;}}
#* '''1856''', {{w|James Planché|J. R. Planché}} (tr.), ''Fairy Tales by the Countess d'Aulnoy'', [[s:Fairy Tales by the Countess d'Aulnoy/The Princess Carpillon|The Princess Carpillon]]:
#* {{RQ:Melville Omoo|passage=One day the cabin steward made me a present of some molasses, which I was so '''choice''' of that I kept it hid away in a tin can in the farthest corner of my bunk.}}
